parts.name: Fortresses razed, roads made safe
parts.summary: Conquest of the western strongholds, deportation and resettlement, the borders extended, and the peace that follows — the famous spindle clause (§35) with its run-up (§33–34) and aftermath (§36–37).

parts.name: The city of Azatiwadaya and its god
parts.summary: Azatiwada builds the fortress and names it after himself, installs Tarhunzas, institutes the yearly offerings, and asks the gods to bless him, the city and its people (Tarhunzas' gifts, §51–52; the people's increase and service to the house of Mopsus, §56–58). §41–47 are damaged; §42, §43, §46 are absent.

parts.name: Curses on whoever erases the name
parts.summary: The protective sanctions: any king or man who erases Azatiwada's name from the gate, covets the fortress, or builds anew with evil intent is handed to the gods; closing wish that the name endure (§74–75).
